question: To coincide with President of the Commission Ms von der Leyen’s nomination as EPP’s lead candidate, the Commission’s DG Comm has just published 56 pages of propaganda trumpeting her achievements. 1.

How does this square with the Commission’s new Code of Conduct which states, in Article 10.5, that the Commission’s human and material resources must not be used for activities linked to the electoral campaign?
What legal consequences is it considering for this wrongful act?
Will Ms von der Leyen personally cover the production costs and personnel expenses incurred in putting together this illustrated brochure and sharing it online?
answer: Subject: Use of the Commission’s material resources in the Commission President’s electoral campaign To coincide with President of the Commission Ms von der Leyen’s nomination as EPP’s lead candidate, the Commission’s DG Comm has just published 56 pages of propaganda trumpeting her achievements. 1. How does this square with the Commission’s new Code of Conduct which states, in Article 10.5, that the Commission’s human and material resources must not be used for activities linked to the electoral campaign? 2.
What legal consequences is it considering for this wrongful act?
3. Will Ms von der Leyen personally cover the production costs and personnel expenses incurred in putting together this illustrated brochure and sharing it online?

Joint answer given by Vice-President Jourová on behalf of the European Commission (20 June 2024) The document mentioned by the Honourable Members in their questions is a publication of the Commission, which presents its achievements under the current mandate. It does not serve the purpose of any specific campaign, party or candidate.

EU institutions have a responsibility to communicate about their activities to EU citizens and other interested parties . The Commission is appointed in the context of a democratic process following the European elections. It is therefore important to give account of its achievements to the citizens of the European Union as has been done in the past by previous Commissions (3).

As every publication of the Commission, it has been prepared with the participation of the dedicated Commission services, ensuring that information about the Commission activities is available in all 24 languages and comprehensive.
